deep.reconstruction:
The page is a printed page, p. 81, of an elementary German algebra textbook. Its handwritten marginal fragments on the left continue Gauss's computation from the facing (previous) page.

PRINTED TEXT (routine definitions of determinate and indeterminate equations):
(a) 4x+6=20 is determinate: x=(20-6)/4. In general ax+b=c gives x=(c-b)/a when a, b, c are known.
(b) x+y=20 is indeterminate unless y is given. Adding x:y=4:1, i.e. x=4y, gives 5y=20, so y=4 and x=16.
(c) Suppose y=(a-x)m=am-mx and x+y=c, so y=c-x. Then am-mx=c-x. Adding mx-c to both sides gives am-c=mx-x=(m-1)x, so x=(am-c)/(m-1).
(d) y could equally be given as a^2, sqrt(a) or log a; in each case x=c-y.
(e) The remaining sections are definitions:
- §172: one needs as many independent equations as unknowns; more makes the system overdetermined.
- §173: definitions of coefficient and term.
- §174: definition of a simple (linear) equation, continued on the next page.

MANUSCRIPT MARGIN (Gauss): the fragments read '…α … η p.', '…6^3 … 1764·6^2/2 … +720·6 …' and '36·41/(720·7) = 41/140'. They are the right-hand ends of lines on the previous page. There Gauss computes the Newton–Cotes weight for 7 nodes (6 subintervals), labelled α…η.

Reconstruction of the computation:
1. With nodes t=0,…,6, the Lagrange weight of the endpoint α is (1/6!) ∫_0^6 (t-1)(t-2)…(t-6) dt; the sign (-1)^6 is +.
2. Expanding the product with Stirling numbers of the first kind (the triangle 1; 1,3,2; 1,6,11,6; … written on the previous page) gives t^6 - 21t^5 + 175t^4 - 735t^3 + 1624t^2 - 1764t + 720.
3. Integrating term by term: [6^7/7 - 21·6^6/6 + 175·6^5/5 - 735·6^4/4 + 1624·6^3/3 - 1764·6^2/2 + 720·6]/720.
4. Gauss factors out 36. The bracket becomes 36×(1110 6/7 - 4536 + 7560 - 6615 + 3248 - 882 + 120).
5. Grouping: positives 12038 6/7, negatives 12033, difference 41/7.
6. Hence the coefficient is 36·41/(720·7) = 41/140. This is the weight per unit step, i.e. per h.

The next page's margin repeats the computation for other nodes ('Corr…'). It also checks that the weights sum to 6: 82+432+54+272=840=6·140. That uses the full weight set (41, 216, 27, 272, 27, 216, 41)/140.
errors: No errors in the printed algebra: from am-mx=c-x, adding mx-c gives am-c=(m-1)x, which is correct (it requires m≠1, unstated).
No errors in Gauss's marginal arithmetic: each term divided by 36 is correct (7776/7, 4536, 7560, 6615, 3248, 882, 120). The sum 41/7 and the result 41/140 are correct.
Minor imprecision in printed §172: 'as many particular equations as unknowns' needs independence/consistency, which is not stated.

results.modern_name: Newton–Cotes quadrature coefficients (closed 7-point rule, weights 41,216,27,272,27,216,41 over 140)

deep.surprise_reason: The printed text is a routine textbook. The marginal computation of Cotes coefficients is standard; Gauss discussed Cotes' coefficients explicitly in his 1814 'Methodus nova integralium valores per approximationem inveniendi', so his computing them is expected.
